tasks.label: Plan and build
tasks.description: Shape an idea, then turn it into working code.

tasks.label: Design interfaces
tasks.description: Visual direction, layout, components and interface quality.

tasks.label: Motion
tasks.description: Web and mobile animation, from first idea to review.

tasks.label: Review and test
tasks.description: Find defects, check flows in a browser and debug failures.

tasks.label: Security
tasks.description: Secure implementation, review and threat modeling.

tasks.label: Ship and deploy
tasks.description: Git, pull requests, releases and hosting.

tasks.label: Docs and files
tasks.description: Markdown, handoffs, office files, notebooks and Notion.

tasks.label: Images and media
tasks.description: Generated images, video, speech and transcription.

tasks.label: Working with agents
tasks.description: How agents load skills, split work and format answers.

startingPoints.task: Build a feature from a rough brief
Get a second opinion on my code
Design a screen that doesn’t look generic
Check a change in a real browser

yeknal-add-changelog.title: Changelog entries
yeknal-add-changelog.purpose: Adds or updates a Keep a Changelog entry based on the changes and history that can actually be verified, so release notes describe what shipped.
whenToUse: You are preparing a release and need the notes written up.
Work has shipped and the changelog has fallen behind.
You want entries grouped the Keep a Changelog way under Added, Changed and Fixed.

example.ask: Add a changelog entry for everything merged since the last tag.
example.outcome: It reads the history since that tag, checks what each change actually did and writes a dated entry grouped by type.

yeknal-agent-cost-control.title: Agent cost control
yeknal-agent-cost-control.purpose: Measures what agent work actually costs, finds the sessions and settings that own the spend, and changes one lever at a time without quietly losing review quality along the way.
whenToUse: The inference bill rose, or one task cost far more than expected.
You are choosing models or effort levels and want evidence rather than a hunch.
Someone asks whether prompt caching, model routing, or a cheaper tier will actually help.
yeknal-agent-cost-control.avoid: It does not decide who does the work and it does not review code. It will not present a saving without an outcome check that nothing important was dropped.

example.ask: Why did last month cost more than the month before, with the same workload?
example.outcome: It reads the harness usage log, shows that one long session carried most of the spend, checks whether caching is already warm, and recommends splitting the work at a boundary instead of switching models.

yeknal-animate.title: Web animation
yeknal-animate.purpose: Adds purposeful, accessible motion to components, pages, scrolling, gestures, SVG and canvas, with sensible timing and a reduced-motion fallback.
whenToUse: You are adding an entrance, transition or gesture to a web interface.
A component needs motion that explains a change instead of decorating it.
You want motion that stays smooth and respects reduced-motion settings.
yeknal-animate.avoid: To audit motion that already exists, use Review animations instead.

example.ask: Animate the settings drawer so it slides in from the right and can be interrupted halfway.
example.outcome: It picks the properties, duration and easing, builds an interruptible transition and adds a reduced-motion version.

attribution.credit: Written for this catalog, drawing on Emil Kowalski’s design-engineering ideas as inspiration; no source was copied.

yeknal-animate-expo.title: Animation in Expo
yeknal-animate-expo.purpose: Builds animation for React Native and Expo apps with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router and haptics, making the decisions that decide whether motion feels right on a device.
whenToUse: You are adding gestures, sheets, screen transitions or press feedback to an Expo app.
Motion stutters on a real device and you need it on the right thread.
You want haptics that match what the interface is doing.
yeknal-animate-expo.avoid: For animation on the web, use Web animation.

example.ask: Make the bottom sheet follow my finger and settle with a spring when I let go.
example.outcome: It wires the drag with Gesture Handler, runs the motion on the UI thread with Reanimated and hands off velocity to a spring.

attribution.credit: Written for this catalog, drawing on Emil Kowalski’s design-engineering ideas as inspiration; no source was copied.

yeknal-animation-vocabulary.title: Animation vocabulary
yeknal-animation-vocabulary.purpose: Turns a vague description of a motion effect into its proper name, so you can ask an agent or a designer for exactly what you mean.
whenToUse: You can describe an effect but don’t know what it’s called.
You want a precise word to put in a prompt or a design brief.
Two people are describing the same motion in different ways.
yeknal-animation-vocabulary.avoid: It names effects; it doesn’t design or build them.

example.ask: What’s it called when a popover sort of bounces as it opens?
example.outcome: It names the effect, explains what makes it look that way and suggests how to describe it in a request.

yeknal-apple-design.title: Apple-style interface design
yeknal-apple-design.purpose: Brings Apple’s approach to fluid, physical motion and interface design to the web, from springs and interruptible gestures to materials, depth and typography.
whenToUse: You are building drag, swipe or sheet interactions that should feel physical.
You want spring animation and momentum that can be interrupted.
Typography, translucency and depth need the restraint Apple interfaces are known for.

example.ask: Review our swipe-to-dismiss card and make it feel more like iOS.
example.outcome: It checks how the gesture tracks the finger, tunes the spring and velocity hand-off and adds a reduced-motion alternative.

yeknal-application-security.title: Application security
yeknal-application-security.purpose: Designs or hardens security across web apps, APIs, cloud setup, CI/CD pipelines and AI features, covering the OWASP-style risks a product is likely to face.
whenToUse: You are building authentication, authorization or an API that handles user data.
A project needs a broad security pass before launch.
You want secure defaults for headers, secrets, rate limits and logging.

example.ask: Harden the API before we launch: auth, rate limiting, headers and how secrets are handled.
example.outcome: It reviews each area against concrete risks, fixes what it can and lists anything that needs a decision from you.

yeknal-ask-sonner.title: Sonner toasts
yeknal-ask-sonner.purpose: A practical guide to Sonner, the React toast library, from wiring up the Toaster to promise toasts, styling, theming and the usual reasons toasts misbehave.
whenToUse: You are adding toast notifications to a React app with Sonner.
Toasts don’t appear, appear twice or sit behind a modal.
Toasts ignore your Tailwind classes or don’t follow dark mode.

example.ask: Show a loading toast while the file uploads, then switch it to success or error.
example.outcome: It sets up a promise toast that updates in place and checks the Toaster is mounted once with the right theme.

attribution.credit: Rewritten for this catalog from an earlier merged UI skill. No upstream author is recorded for it.

yeknal-aspnet-core.title: ASP.NET Core
yeknal-aspnet-core.purpose: Builds, reviews and upgrades ASP.NET Core applications using current official guidance, from Blazor and Razor Pages to Minimal APIs, SignalR and authentication.
whenToUse: You are working on a Blazor, Razor Pages, MVC or Web API project.
Middleware, dependency injection or configuration needs to follow current guidance.
You are planning an ASP.NET Core upgrade.

example.ask: Add a Minimal API endpoint for orders with validation and proper authorization.
example.outcome: It follows the project’s existing conventions, adds the endpoint with validation and policy-based authorization, and notes how to test it.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Microsoft’s ASP.NET Core skill.

yeknal-brainstorm.title: Brainstorm
yeknal-brainstorm.purpose: Generates and compares genuinely different approaches before anything is built, which helps when the problem is still fuzzy.
whenToUse: You have a problem but no settled approach.
You want more than one option before committing time to building.
The brief is ambiguous and needs framing first.

example.ask: Give me three different ways to let users undo a bulk delete, with the trade-offs.
example.outcome: It sketches distinct approaches, compares effort and risk, and recommends one with its reasons.

yeknal-brandkit.title: Brand kit images
yeknal-brandkit.purpose: Generates polished brand-guideline boards, logo systems and identity presentations as images, with deliberate composition and sparse typography.
whenToUse: You want visual concepts for a new brand or product identity.
You need a brand-guidelines board to share with a team.
You are exploring logo directions before committing to one.
yeknal-brandkit.requirements: Needs an image-generation tool available to your agent.

example.ask: Create a brand board for a calm budgeting app: logo ideas, palette and type.
example.outcome: It plans the identity, then generates a board with logo concepts, colours, type and a couple of mockups.

yeknal-break-ui.title: Break UI
yeknal-break-ui.purpose: Stress-tests a screen with realistic worst-case data, such as long names, missing fields, huge counts and non-Latin text, and reports every break with its fix.
whenToUse: A screen looks fine with demo data and you want to know where it fails.
You are about to ship a list, table or card that shows user-supplied text.
You want a dev-only toggle between demo and worst-case states.

example.ask: Try the worst case on the team members table.
example.outcome: It fills the table with extreme but realistic data, shows the broken states and fixes overflow, wrapping and empty values.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Emil Kowalski’s skills collection.

yeknal-chatgpt-apps.title: ChatGPT apps
yeknal-chatgpt-apps.purpose: Builds and troubleshoots ChatGPT Apps SDK projects that pair an MCP server with a widget UI, starting from the current official documentation.
whenToUse: You are scaffolding a new ChatGPT app.
You need to register UI resources or wire the MCP Apps bridge.
Metadata, CSP or domain settings are getting in the way.
yeknal-chatgpt-apps.requirements: Written with Codex in mind and works best alongside the OpenAI docs skill.

example.ask: Scaffold a ChatGPT app that searches our recipes and shows results in a widget.
example.outcome: It checks the current docs, sets up the MCP server and tools, and registers the widget with the right metadata.

yeknal-cleanup.title: Cleanup
yeknal-cleanup.purpose: Removes dead code, stale dependencies and redundant configuration once it has confirmed they really are unused.
whenToUse: A project has accumulated files and packages nobody uses.
You want to prune configuration that no longer does anything.
You are tidying up after a large refactor.

example.ask: Clean up unused dependencies and leftover config from the old build setup.
example.outcome: It proves each item is unused before removing it, then runs the build and tests to confirm nothing broke.

yeknal-cloudflare-deploy.title: Cloudflare deploy
yeknal-cloudflare-deploy.purpose: Deploys applications and infrastructure to Cloudflare using Workers, Pages and related services, with references for the platform’s products.
whenToUse: You want to host a site or API on Cloudflare.
You are setting up Workers, Pages, KV or R2 for a project.
A Cloudflare deployment needs configuring or fixing.
yeknal-cloudflare-deploy.requirements: Uses Wrangler and needs a Cloudflare account or API token.

example.ask: Deploy this Astro site to Cloudflare Pages with a preview for every branch.
example.outcome: It configures the project for Pages, deploys it with Wrangler and gives you the preview and production URLs.

yeknal-content-seo.title: Content and SEO
yeknal-content-seo.purpose: Guides useful content and search visibility together, from keyword patterns and page briefs to metadata, structured data, sitemaps, local search, earned links and AI citations.
whenToUse: You are choosing which queries to target and which pages should exist.
You are planning or rewriting pages and want them to be found.
Metadata, canonical tags, crawlability or structured data need an audit.
A local business is invisible in the map pack, or links and coverage need a plan.
Traffic moved and you need to separate a ranking loss from a click-through loss.
You want a site to be readable by search engines and AI search alike.

example.ask: Choose the queries worth targeting and tell me whether to update an existing page or create a new one.
example.outcome: It reads the live results, checks existing query and page data, and returns a decision, a brief and the evidence behind it.

yeknal-dead-code-hunter.title: Dead code hunter
yeknal-dead-code-hunter.purpose: Finds and removes dead code, unused imports, unreachable branches and variables nobody reads, across Python, TypeScript, JavaScript and other languages.
whenToUse: You want a code-health scan before a refactor.
Linters keep flagging unused imports and symbols.
You suspect branches that can never run.

example.ask: Scan the services folder for unused exports and unreachable code.
example.outcome: It lists each finding with evidence, removes the safe ones and flags anything that might be used dynamically.

yeknal-design-reference-research.title: Design reference research
yeknal-design-reference-research.purpose: Researches comparable products and collects references into an evidence ledger and brief, so design decisions come from what works rather than what’s fashionable.
whenToUse: You are about to design or redesign something and want evidence first.
The team disagrees about direction and needs references to compare.
You want patterns from real products, not gallery trends.

example.ask: Research how five scheduling apps handle rescheduling before we redesign ours.
example.outcome: It studies each flow, records what it saw and what it couldn’t verify, and writes a short brief with recommendations.

yeknal-design-taste-frontend.title: Design taste for the web
yeknal-design-taste-frontend.purpose: Designs and builds expressive landing pages, portfolios and marketing sites from real product evidence instead of reusable AI layouts.
whenToUse: A new web experience needs distinctive art direction and working code.
You want a landing page that doesn’t look like a template.
The brand has a story the layout should carry.
yeknal-design-taste-frontend.avoid: For an existing product, use Redesign an existing product instead.

example.ask: Design and build a launch page for our note-taking app that feels like ours.
example.outcome: It pulls the visual direction from the product itself, then builds a responsive page with real copy and states.

yeknal-design-taste-frontend-v1.title: Design taste for the web (v1)
yeknal-design-taste-frontend-v1.purpose: The original version of the design-taste skill, kept for projects that depend on its exact behaviour.
whenToUse: A project was built around the v1 skill and must keep behaving the same.
You need to reproduce results from the earlier version.
yeknal-design-taste-frontend-v1.avoid: For new work, use Design taste for the web, which replaces this version.

example.ask: Keep using the v1 taste rules for this older landing page.
example.outcome: It applies the original v1 guidance so the page stays consistent with what was built before.

yeknal-develop-web-game.title: Web game development
yeknal-develop-web-game.purpose: Gives your agent a reliable loop for building browser games: make a small change, play it through a Playwright script, then check screenshots and console errors.
whenToUse: You are building or iterating on an HTML and JavaScript game.
Changes keep breaking gameplay and you want each one checked.
You need deterministic frame stepping for automated play.
yeknal-develop-web-game.requirements: Written with Codex in mind and needs Playwright available.

example.ask: Add a double jump to the platformer and make sure nothing else broke.
example.outcome: It implements the change, plays through the level with scripted input, inspects screenshots and fixes any console errors.

yeknal-doc.title: Word documents
yeknal-doc.purpose: Reads, creates and edits .docx files where formatting matters, and renders pages to check the layout visually.
whenToUse: You need a Word document generated or edited.
Layout fidelity matters, such as headings, tables and page breaks.
You want to check how a document actually renders.
yeknal-doc.requirements: Uses Python with python-docx, and Poppler or LibreOffice for rendering checks.

example.ask: Turn these meeting notes into a formatted Word report with a table of actions.
example.outcome: It builds the document with proper styles and a table, renders it and fixes any layout problems.

yeknal-domain-modeling.title: Domain modeling
yeknal-domain-modeling.purpose: Clarifies a project’s domain terms and boundaries and records the decisions in a glossary or architecture decision record.
whenToUse: People use different words for the same thing, or one word for two things.
System boundaries are unclear before a larger change.
You want a GLOSSARY.md or an ADR written down.

example.ask: We keep mixing up accounts, workspaces and organisations. Sort out the terms.
example.outcome: It maps how each term is used in code and conversation, proposes definitions and records them in a glossary.

attribution.credit: Written independently, inspired by the domain-modeling skill in Matt Pocock’s skills collection; no source text was copied.

yeknal-emil-design-eng.title: Design engineering polish
yeknal-emil-design-eng.purpose: Applies the careful interaction details and purposeful motion that Emil Kowalski is known for, so components feel considered rather than merely functional.
whenToUse: A component works but doesn’t feel finished.
You are reviewing hover, press and focus details.
You want motion that supports the interaction rather than decorating it.

example.ask: Polish the command menu so opening, filtering and selecting feel crisp.
example.outcome: It tightens timing and easing, adds proper press and focus states and removes motion that slows people down.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Emil Kowalski’s skills collection.

yeknal-engineering-specialists.title: Engineering specialists
yeknal-engineering-specialists.purpose: Routes implementation through focused guidance for the framework, language, API, data, build, CLI, realtime or deployment problem in front of you.
whenToUse: The work crosses several parts of the stack.
You want the agent to apply specialist knowledge for a particular framework or layer.
A change touches data, APIs and the interface at once.

example.ask: Add realtime updates to the dashboard using our existing WebSocket server.
example.outcome: It applies realtime and frontend guidance together, wires the updates and handles reconnects and stale data.

yeknal-figma-implement-design.title: Figma to code
yeknal-figma-implement-design.purpose: Turns Figma frames into production code that matches the design closely, using the Figma MCP server for design context, screenshots and assets.
whenToUse: You have a Figma URL or node ID to implement.
A component must match its Figma spec exactly.
You want design tokens translated into the project’s own conventions.
yeknal-figma-implement-design.requirements: Needs a working Figma MCP server connection.

example.ask: Implement this Figma frame as a React component using our design tokens.
example.outcome: It reads the frame through the Figma MCP server, maps values to existing tokens and builds the component to match.

yeknal-finalize.title: Finalize
yeknal-finalize.purpose: Runs the final documentation and quality checks, summarises the diff and handles any Git publishing you asked for.
whenToUse: The work is done and needs a last check before delivery.
You want a clear summary of what changed.
You are ready to commit and push but want the gates run first.

example.ask: Finalize this branch: run the checks, update the docs and push it.
example.outcome: It runs the repository’s checks, updates documentation that the change affects, summarises the diff and pushes.

yeknal-find-animation-opportunities.title: Find animation opportunities
yeknal-find-animation-opportunities.purpose: Looks through a codebase or interface for places that should animate and rejects those that shouldn’t, proposing motion with exact values but changing nothing.
whenToUse: You wonder what could be animated in an app.
An interface feels static and you want it to feel more alive.
You want proposals before anyone writes animation code.
yeknal-find-animation-opportunities.avoid: To fix existing animation, use Improve animations or Review animations.

example.ask: What in the onboarding flow would benefit from motion?
example.outcome: It lists a few specific opportunities with durations and easing, and explains why other spots should stay still.

attribution.credit: Written for this catalog, drawing on Emil Kowalski’s design-engineering ideas as inspiration; no source was copied.

yeknal-frontend-design.title: Frontend design
yeknal-frontend-design.purpose: Sets a distinctive visual direction for new or heavily reshaped UI, from typography and composition to palette and interface copy.
whenToUse: You are designing a new screen or product surface.
A design looks generic and needs a clear point of view.
Typography, colour and layout need to work as one system.

example.ask: Design the pricing page so it doesn’t look like every other SaaS template.
example.outcome: It sets a visual direction from the product’s content, picks type and colour roles and builds the page with real copy.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Anthropic’s frontend-design skill. Its library guidance credits Rare UI, which requires attribution if you install one of its components.

yeknal-frontend-developer.title: Frontend developer
yeknal-frontend-developer.purpose: Implements or repairs accessible web interfaces in React, Vue or Angular, covering components, state, styling and browser behaviour.
whenToUse: You are changing frontend components or their state.
A browser behaviour or styling bug needs fixing.
You want accessible, working UI rather than a visual concept.

example.ask: Fix the date picker so it works with the keyboard and screen readers.
example.outcome: It repairs focus handling and labels, tests the keyboard path and keeps the existing look.

yeknal-full-output-enforcement.title: Full output
yeknal-full-output-enforcement.purpose: Makes the agent return complete code or documents without placeholder gaps, splitting long output only at real boundaries.
whenToUse: You need every line of a file, not a summary with ellipses.
Earlier answers left out sections with placeholders.
Output is long enough that it has to be split carefully.
yeknal-full-output-enforcement.avoid: It only runs when you explicitly ask for exhaustive output.

example.ask: Give me the full migration file, every line, no placeholders.
example.outcome: It writes the complete file and, if it has to split it, breaks at clear boundaries and says where to continue.

yeknal-gh-address-comments.title: Address PR comments
yeknal-gh-address-comments.purpose: Works through the review and issue comments on the open GitHub pull request for your current branch, using the GitHub CLI.
whenToUse: A pull request has review comments waiting.
You want each comment addressed or answered in turn.
You use the gh CLI and want the agent to read the PR directly.
yeknal-gh-address-comments.requirements: Needs the GitHub CLI signed in to your account.

example.ask: Address the review comments on my PR.
example.outcome: It checks gh is signed in, reads each comment, makes the changes and summarises what it did for each one.

yeknal-gh-fix-ci.title: Fix failing CI
yeknal-gh-fix-ci.purpose: Inspects failing GitHub Actions checks on a pull request, summarises the logs, drafts a fix plan and only makes changes once you approve.
whenToUse: Checks are failing on a pull request.
You want the failure explained before anything changes.
CI runs on GitHub Actions.
yeknal-gh-fix-ci.avoid: Checks from other providers, such as Buildkite, are reported by link only.
yeknal-gh-fix-ci.requirements: Needs the GitHub CLI signed in to your account.

example.ask: The tests job is failing on my PR. Find out why.
example.outcome: It pulls the failing job’s logs, explains the cause, proposes a fix and waits for your go-ahead.

yeknal-git.title: Git
yeknal-git.purpose: Handles status, diffs, branches, commits, merges and pushes while leaving unrelated work in your checkout alone.
whenToUse: You want a focused commit without sweeping in other changes.
You need help with a branch, merge or history question.
Your working tree has unrelated edits that must survive.

example.ask: Commit only the API changes and push them to a new branch.
example.outcome: It stages just those files, writes a clear commit message, creates the branch and pushes it.

yeknal-gpt-taste.title: GPT taste (compatibility)
yeknal-gpt-taste.purpose: Kept so older requests for gpt-taste still work. It hands premium art direction over to High-end visual design.
whenToUse: An existing prompt or project still asks for gpt-taste by name.
yeknal-gpt-taste.avoid: For new work, use High-end visual design directly.

example.ask: Use gpt-taste for this hero section.
example.outcome: It routes the request to the current high-end visual design guidance instead of the retired recipe.

yeknal-high-end-visual-design.title: High-end visual design
yeknal-high-end-visual-design.purpose: Creates art-directed, showcase-level web interfaces with a product-specific visual idea, expressive type, deliberate composition and considered motion.
whenToUse: The brief explicitly asks for agency, editorial or experimental quality.
A launch or showcase page needs a strong visual idea.
Ordinary product styling isn’t enough for this piece.
yeknal-high-end-visual-design.avoid: For everyday product UI, use Frontend design instead.

example.ask: Art-direct the launch page for our camera app as if it were a magazine feature.
example.outcome: It develops a visual thesis from the product, then builds a page with editorial type, imagery and restrained motion.

yeknal-human-ai-interface-design.title: Human-AI interface design
yeknal-human-ai-interface-design.purpose: Designs AI features people can trust, covering suggestions, generation, copilots and agents, along with sources, uncertainty, approvals and recovery.
whenToUse: You are adding an AI feature to a product.
Users need to see where an answer came from or how sure it is.
An agent can take actions that need approval or undo.

example.ask: Design how our assistant proposes calendar changes before it makes them.
example.outcome: It designs a review step with clear sources, editable proposals, approval and a way to undo.

yeknal-i-have-adhd.title: ADHD-friendly answers
yeknal-i-have-adhd.purpose: Shapes answers into short, action-first steps with visible progress, which can make long tasks easier to follow.
whenToUse: You prefer answers that lead with the next action.
Long explanations make it hard to keep track.
You want progress shown clearly as work moves along.
yeknal-i-have-adhd.avoid: It only runs when you turn it on by asking for it.

example.ask: ADHD mode on. Help me set up the project locally.
example.outcome: It answers with one clear step at a time, keeps the current state visible and skips long preambles.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Ayoub Ghriss’s i-have-adhd skill.

yeknal-image-to-code.title: Image to code
yeknal-image-to-code.purpose: Studies an approved screenshot or concept image, works out its visual and responsive system, and builds the frontend to match it faithfully.
whenToUse: You have a screenshot or mockup to turn into code.
An approved concept must be implemented without drifting.
You want the responsive behaviour worked out from a static image.
yeknal-image-to-code.avoid: It won’t replace an approved reference with a newly generated design.

example.ask: Build this landing page screenshot as a responsive Astro page.
example.outcome: It extracts spacing, type and colour from the image, then builds the page and checks it at phone and desktop widths.

yeknal-imagegen.title: Image generation
yeknal-imagegen.purpose: Generates and edits images through the OpenAI Image API, including masks, background removal, transparent backgrounds and batches of variants.
whenToUse: You need product shots, covers or concept art.
An image needs inpainting or its background replaced.
You want several variants generated in one go.
yeknal-imagegen.requirements: Uses Python and needs an OPENAI_API_KEY for live calls.

example.ask: Make three cover images for the blog post with a transparent background.
example.outcome: It writes the prompts, runs the bundled script and saves the variants for you to choose from.

yeknal-imagegen-frontend-mobile.title: Mobile app concept images
yeknal-imagegen-frontend-mobile.purpose: Generates polished concept images of mobile app screens and flows inside a phone frame, with consistent hierarchy across screens. It creates images, not code.
whenToUse: You want to see a mobile app idea before building it.
Several screens need to look like one consistent product.
You need concepts for iOS, Android or both.
yeknal-imagegen-frontend-mobile.requirements: Needs an image-generation tool available to your agent.

example.ask: Show me the onboarding and home screens for a plant-care app.
example.outcome: It plans the flow, then generates consistent screen concepts framed in a phone mockup.

yeknal-imagegen-frontend-web.title: Website concept images
yeknal-imagegen-frontend-web.purpose: Generates website concept images for landing pages and sections that developers can actually read and build from.
whenToUse: You want visual concepts for a site rather than code.
A page needs its section order worked out from real content.
Developers need section-sized images with readable detail.
yeknal-imagegen-frontend-web.requirements: Needs an image-generation tool available to your agent.

example.ask: Give me concept images for a landing page for our invoicing tool.
example.outcome: It works out the page sections from your content and generates readable images for each one.

yeknal-implement.title: Implement
yeknal-implement.purpose: Takes a scoped feature or fix from plan to working code while keeping the rest of the repository behaving as it did.
whenToUse: You want a feature built or a bug fixed from start to finish.
The change has to fit existing conventions and not break other behaviour.
You want the work verified rather than just written.

example.ask: Add CSV export to the reports page.
example.outcome: It reads how the page works today, adds the export following existing patterns and runs the flow to confirm it works.

yeknal-improve-animations.title: Improve animations
yeknal-improve-animations.purpose: Surveys an app’s existing motion like a senior motion designer would, then writes a prioritised audit with self-contained plans that other agents can carry out.
whenToUse: You want a roadmap of animation fixes across an app.
Motion feels inconsistent and you don’t know where to start.
You plan to hand the fixes to other agents or a cheaper model.
yeknal-improve-animations.avoid: It plans changes but doesn’t edit source code.

example.ask: Audit the motion across the dashboard and plan what to fix first.
example.outcome: It inventories each animation, ranks the problems and writes a standalone fix plan for each.

attribution.credit: Written for this catalog, drawing on Emil Kowalski’s design-engineering ideas as inspiration; no source was copied.

yeknal-industrial-brutalist-ui.title: Industrial brutalist UI

yeknal-launch-readiness.title: Launch readiness
yeknal-launch-readiness.purpose: Audits a product before it becomes publicly reachable, covering the legal obligations that attach to the data, payments, email and user content it handles, plus the engineering gates no other workflow owns, then returns one register and a go or no-go.

yeknal-legacy-sweep.title: Legacy sweep

yeknal-ui-ux-designer.purpose: Designs user-centred interface systems that balance intuitive flows with a distinctive visual direction, from information architecture to interaction patterns.
whenToUse: You are shaping how a product is organised and navigated.
A flow is confusing and needs rethinking.
You need a UI specification someone can build from.

example.ask: Rethink how people find and manage saved reports.
example.outcome: It maps the current flow, proposes a clearer structure and specifies the screens and interactions.

yeknal-vercel-deploy.title: Vercel deploy
yeknal-vercel-deploy.purpose: Deploys applications and websites to Vercel and gives you the link, with preview deploys by default and production when you ask.
whenToUse: You want an app online quickly.
You need a preview link to share.
A project is ready to go to production on Vercel.
yeknal-vercel-deploy.requirements: Uses the Vercel CLI and a Vercel account.

example.ask: Deploy this and give me the link.
example.outcome: It checks for the Vercel CLI, runs a preview deploy and returns the URL.

yeknal-verification-audit.title: Verification audit
yeknal-verification-audit.purpose: Keeps a project's verification skill and feature map honest by rechecking every feature against source, driving every feature in one live session, and shipping only proven corrections.
whenToUse: A verification skill or feature map has fallen behind the app.
You want every mapped feature exercised live, not just skimmed.
You need one clear outcome: clean, changed or blocked.
yeknal-verification-audit.avoid: It never edits product code; a real regression is reported, not fixed here.

example.ask: Audit the verify skill before we cut the release.
example.outcome: It reads each feature from source, drives all of them in one session, fixes stale map entries and reports what is actually broken.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Lauren Tan's pstack skill of the same name.

yeknal-verification-harness.title: Verification harness
yeknal-verification-harness.purpose: Generates a project-local skill that launches the real app, drives a feature the way a user would, and captures proof, with a feature map for the next agent to follow.
whenToUse: A repository has no scripted way to prove its UI, CLI or service behavior.
You are tired of re-deriving how to start the app and check a flow.
You want screenshots, transcripts or response bodies kept as evidence.
yeknal-verification-harness.avoid: It builds the harness; for what counts as proof, use Testing strategy.

example.ask: This repo has no way to prove a flow end to end. Set one up.
example.outcome: It inspects how the app starts and can be driven, writes a verify skill with launch, doctor, drive, evidence and cleanup, seeds a feature map and then proves it once.

attribution.credit: Adapted from Lauren Tan's pstack skill of the same name.

whenToUse: You are starting a new Windows desktop app.
A machine needs setting up for WinUI development.
XAML controls, navigation or theming need work.

example.outcome: It checks the environment, scaffolds the app and sets up navigation and theming the recommended way.

yeknal-write-swift.title: Modern Swift
yeknal-write-swift.purpose: Writes and reviews modern Swift, including value types, Swift 6 data-race safety, concurrency, generics, API design, performance and Swift Testing.
whenToUse: You are writing or migrating Swift code.
A concurrency error, hang or data race needs fixing.
You want Swift that uses current language features well.

example.ask: Fix the data-race warnings after enabling Swift 6 mode.
example.outcome: It explains each warning, applies the right isolation or actor changes and keeps behaviour the same.

yeknal-yeet.title: Commit, push and open a PR
yeknal-yeet.purpose: Stages, commits, pushes and opens a GitHub pull request in one flow using the GitHub CLI.
whenToUse: You want the whole commit-to-PR flow done in one go.
Your changes are ready and reviewed locally.
You use the gh CLI.
